source_commit_note: 05e95b1 is not on main. Its code outside the tests is equal to 5078afd, so each non-test site in this record has the same line at 5078afd. The runs used 05e95b1 with the test changes of this record applied: the new file internal/session/coupling_cap_test.go and the corrected TestCouplingRemoteHTTPRejectsUnqualifiedFields were not in 05e95b1. The rerun of u4-startup-cancel used f186580, where the mutated line is also persist.go:278. On main the new test file names the third member of composedShape, which main added after 05e95b1.
scope: The format rows of the coupling qualification plan (G8, G9, C1, C3, C4, C5, U3, U4, U7) at the single save and stream family (save 9, hello 6). The simulation motion rows are not in this record. The follow-up at 39f05af adds the WASM and browser runs (G8) and the format cost and heap numbers (G9 measurements), which also serve U5 for the formats.
method: Each mutation replaced one anchor, which occurs once in the file at the source commit, in a copy of the file. go test -overlay compiled the mutant; the source tree did not change. The record gives the sha256 of the file before the run, and the file had the same hash after the run.

Each mutation had a passing control run of the same tests, a mutant that compiled, and a mutant run. KILLED means that the mutant run failed on an assertion of the named test. SURVIVED means that the mutant run passed. VOID means a compile failure or a failure for another reason; there are no VOID results.

Commands: go test -p 2 -count=1 -run <tests> <package> for the control; go test -c -overlay=<overlay> then <binary> -test.run <tests> -test.count=1 -test.v for the mutant. Each run had ulimit -v 16000000, nice -n 19 and GOMAXPROCS=4.

A mutation that survived its named tests also ran against all tests of the session package (except TestComposedWorstCaseFormats and TestCouplingSaveCapRejectsAtomically, which are the two large fixtures), and of the remote package for client-side guards. These wider runs share one control run of the same command, which passed.
The plan names guards by their line at 069bafb. Items 4, 5 and 7 moved them; each site below is the line at the source commit.

browser.setup: go generate ./... built dist at 39f05af. cmd/serve ran on 127.0.0.1 with -dir dist and -state file://<dir>, where the store held the phase fixture save occupied-false-phase-1-leg-0.json (one group, phase closing, not paused). A Node 24 script drove the page /game.html over the Chrome DevTools Protocol with the built-in WebSocket. A script that runs at document start wraps podsimStreamDiagnostic, so it counts the stream events of the Go/WASM client. A loop read /api/state every 3 s.
browser.result: Pass. In 150 s, the client made 1 connection and applied 1 full frame and 2,945 delta frames, with 120 heartbeats, no disconnection, and no console message or exception. The mean apply time was 4.34 ms and the maximum was 104 ms. The server group went through closing, latching (tick 1,046), connected (1,228), unlatching (3,226), opening (3,408) and draining (4,316), and it retired by tick 7,405, after which no cabin had a coupling ID. The client applied each of these changes as a delta.
notes: Chromium stopped with a trace trap under ulimit -v 16000000, so the browser ran with nice -n 19 only. The server and the driver ran with the cap.
The run is the headless shell with SwiftShader, with one group. It does not check the drawing.

measurements.reading: The client decode of a coupled publication costs about 0.7 to 0.9 ms of CPU, and most of it is the token scans before the typed decode. The server encode of a one-tick delta costs about 72 us. The decoded values keep 5 to 12 KB, also when the input is at the 65 MiB cap. rows.requirement: Combined widest limits: sites, corridors, groups, pods, Express orders and project padding together across project, save (raw and gzip), stream (JSON and binary), topology, HTTP and commands.
rows.result: Covered except the command body. Save raw and gzip, full and delta JSON, and HTTP with the topology at its cap are measured. Groups (150), pods (300), Express orders and the project at its 10 MiB byte cap are in the fixtures. Sites and corridors are not in the fixtures, because the fixture network has no valid geometry; the project member is at its byte cap whatever it holds, and the HTTP bound sets the topology to its cap, so sites and corridors cannot make the measured documents larger. The binary stream frame is the gzip form of the JSON: the composed test makes it with compressStreamJSON, which checks MaxStreamMessage, and TestStreamGzipExpansionBound shows that 64 MiB of incompressible JSON gives 67,114,009 bytes, below 68,157,440.

notes: HTTP state has no context check, and this round adds none. The handler only reads the session: it holds the session lock to copy the topology and the frame, and it encodes after it releases the lock. A cancel can only waste one encode, which the HTTP cap bounds, and the reply write then fails. The receipt pins this behavior; a context check before the encode would save that work but is not needed for correctness.

The startup save receipt uses a fake store that checks its context, as the file store does. A store that ignores its context could still write the state after startup returned. The production bucket store passes the context to the bucket write.

open_gaps.gap: Some caps outside the session decode chain have no over-cap test at their caller and survive because an earlier or later cap refuses the same input, or because no input reaches them: the compressed save writer cap, the stream encode caps of EncodeStreamJSON and streamEncoder.encode, the compressed stream cap, the HTTP encode and topology caps, the HTTP topology scan cap, and the half-fleet group check; see the readings of the surviving mutations.

No command is measured with the widest coupled project. The bound holds by construction: project.Validate limits the compact project JSON to project.MaxFileBytes, and MaxInflatedCommandBytes is project.MaxFileBytes plus 64 KiB. TestCommandCouplingArrayBounds checks the counts only.
The composed fixtures have no coupling sites or corridors, because the fixture network has no valid geometry. The byte bound holds because the project member and the topology are at their byte caps.

The cancellation receipts and the cost numbers use the phase fixture with one group. The only coupled save that the restore accepts is the native phase fixture, with 11 nodes, 13 lanes, 3 stations, 2 sites and 1 corridor. 150 copies of it, for 150 groups and 300 pods, would need 450 stations, more than project.MaxStations (300). A fixture with the widest coupled assets needs a native generator in internal/sim, which this round did not change.
